summary: Original site of a 1938 Forestry Commission Aermotor tower near Bonneau, Berkeley County; sold, moved to Sumter County and re-erected on private land.

facts.design: Aermotor LS-40 steel tower, 100 ft, with 7 by 7 foot steel cab
facts.status_note: Sold and moved from this site; the sale date varies by source. Now on private land in Sumter County

access.note: The tower now stands on the owner's private land in Sumter County; no public access is described

events.note: Aermotor LS-40 erected near Bonneau, Berkeley County, for the SC Forestry Commission
SC Forestry Commission closed its fire tower system on October 1, 1993 (system-wide)
Registered February 24, 2013 as US 968, SC 21; the listing describes the structure now in Sumter County

evidence.supports: built 1938 as a 100-foot Aermotor LS-40 steel tower with a 7x7 cab
evidence.quote: 1938: A 100-foot Aermotor LS-40 steel tower with 7x7 cab erected.

evidence.supports: agency and county: Forestry Commission, Berkeley County
evidence.quote: South Carolina - Berkeley County - South Carolina Forestry Commission

evidence.supports: originally located near Bonneau in Berkeley County
evidence.quote: Built in 1938, this 100' Aermotor LS-40 steel tower with 7'x7' steel cab was originally located near the town of Bonneau, SC in Berkeley County.

evidence.supports: operator time in the cab set by fire danger; up to ten hours a day at high danger
evidence.quote: when danger was high, they might spend as much as ten hours per day in the cab

evidence.supports: operator hours in the cab depended on the fire danger
register titles the Sumter County tower the Bonneau Tower

evidence.quote: The Forestry Commission closed its fire tower system on October 1, 1993.

evidence.supports: sold to a private party, moved, sale year given as 199??
evidence.quote: 199??: The tower was sold to a private party, moved and erected at a private location.

evidence.supports: bought by McIntosh in the late 1990s, moved to Sumter County, re-erected
evidence.quote: The tower was purchased from the SC Forestry Commission by Billy McIntosh in the late 1990s and moved to Sumter County, reconditioned, and re-erected on Mr McIntosh's property.

evidence.supports: state commissioned McIntosh to relocate one tower after towers came up for auction in the early 2000s
evidence.quote: Shortly after the towers became available for auction in the early 2000s, Billy McIntosh, a now-retired heavy equipment contractor, was commissioned by the state of South Carolina to relocate one of the towers.

evidence.supports: the structure now stands in Sumter County

corrections.why: Both sources say the tower was sold and moved away from the original Bonneau site to a private location in Sumter County

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Forest Lookouts gives only 199?? with question marks; the register says the late 1990s; a magazine feature places the state's request to move a tower in the early 2000s, shortly after towers became available for auction

sources.title: Bonneau Tower, National Historic Lookout Register

notes_for_editor: Original-site record. The same tower is covered at its current Sumter County site in us-sc-bonneau, so the two records should be linked. The move is not logged as an event because the sale year is disputed (199??, late 1990s, early 2000s). The magazine says two of McIntosh's towers stood at an original 110 feet, while the register gives this tower 100 feet; the magazine does not say which tower is which, so the height gap is not used in the story. The record's coordinates (33.3171, -79.951) are not checked against any source. The P&C article reports the system decommissioned in 1994; the SCFC page says closed 1993, and this story follows SCFC. The magazine quotes McIntosh recalling that the state would not pay him to move the towers but he could have them, which does not square with the register's purchase; the story attributes the purchase to the register only.
